CONF1.question: A liquid-scintillator detector has a fiducial volume of 165 m3 in which 99.8% of the hydrogen atoms are deuterium. That leaves about 1.2e26 hydrogen-1 atoms, 6e28 deuterium atoms and 2.9e29 electrons per cubic metre. An electron-antineutrino emitter of about 1e2 kCi sits 7.5 m from the centre of the fiducial volume. Its continuous energy spectrum ends at 3.0 MeV. The emitter's mean life is about 400 days. Within 18 months, counting all interaction channels together (inverse beta decay on hydrogen-1, charged-current and neutral-current reactions on deuterium, and elastic scattering on electrons), can the detector record at least 1500 interactions from this emitter such that the individual neutrino energy is reconstructed to within 10% for at least 80% of them? End your answer with one line: VERDICT: YES or VERDICT: NO.
